note: v1: TWO FLOORS, tribal / percussive warehouse techno where one bar holds two tempos. A 12-step pivot grid (triplet eighths) carries a shekere on every step, congas and an agogo line; under the MACHINE's floor (a 909 four-on-the-floor, steps 0 3 6 9) those twelve steps are a tribal shuffle at 128, under the TRIBE's floor (deep driven toms, three to the bar on 0 4 8) they are straight sixteenths at 96, and nothing about the tempo or the bar changes. The form walks between them: the groove in four (clap, open hats, a rolling G-minor bass galloping between the kicks, a Gm9 stab through a comb already sitting on the three-floor's off-beats); BOTH floors at once (4 against 3, the ear can stand on either); the 909 leaves and the bar SLOWS to 96 (clap, rim and hats move to the three); the break with no floor at all, the shekere's accents flipping between 4 and 3 every two bars over a drone and a Shepard riser (a Necker cube for tempo); then the drop: the four slamming back, with a distorted 909 layer, on top of the three. Mixed against the album: the first render was +8 to +18 dB heavy at 32-155 Hz (rumble and sub), cut; a hot master with parallel saturation and the set's dynamics after it (rms -12.9, crest 9.1). Seeds 0/11: 95.64 / 95.44 (variety 79 is the weak term: the limiter keeps the section range near 8 dB).
next: Widen the dynamics (variety 79): a real drop-out before the drop, or the slow section stripped to toms and shekere; give the tribe's floor more weight (a chest-hit tom kick); a hypnotic mutation in the long groove.

note: v2: the TRIBE GETS ITS CHEST and the set gets its contrast. Each of the toms' three-to-the-bar hits now has an 808 boom under it at the same pitch (D2 D2 A1), driven, so the tribe's floor hits as hard as the machine's, and the sustained 808 sub steps aside wherever the toms play (the boom is the low end there; the spectrum held at 95.3). The break got emptier: after the four drone bars the shekere plays ONLY its accents, four or three hits a bar, still flipping between the floors every two bars, so the Necker cube is bare bones, and bar 96 is a BLACKOUT, nothing but the riser's tail: the floor vanishes, then the four slams back over the three. And the slow section opens bare (toms, boom, shekere and the three-floor backbeat; the rolling bass re-enters at bar 69), so the slowing lands as a reveal. Seeds 0/11 (pin 3c2c411f; v1 byte-identical): 95.642 / 95.436 -> 97.579 / 97.325, variety 79 -> 90 (density cv .10 -> .15).
next: Harry's notes; a hypnotic mutation through the long groove (the stab's filter or the conga line evolving); maybe a formant-pitched vocal chop (wM's new pitch.formant) on the three-floor; widen the level range (still ~8 dB).
